title: A Playlist for the Yearbook
premise: Hazel Joubert, the overlooked statistician of her high school basketball team, discovers that the numbers she tracks are quietly rewriting reality — every stat she logs bends the world toward the team's survival, and someone has been feeding her rigged data. When she finds impossible instructions in her late grandmother's recipe box, Hazel learns the championship game is a ritual her grandmother once played to keep their town from fading out of existence, and this year the recipe is incomplete. To finish it, Hazel must choose between exposing the rigging that made her complicit and playing the final quarter herself, trading her anonymity — and possibly her memory of who she is — for everyone else's belonging. She wins the game that doesn't matter by losing the one that does, and in the last scene writes her own name into the yearbook for the first time.
about_author: Astrid Winterbourne is a former sports statistician who grew up in a small town where Friday night games were the only thing anyone agreed on. She writes stories about quiet kids who keep score of everything except themselves.

chapters.title: Box Score
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. From the bleachers' edge, Hazel logs stats no one reads and notices the team only wins when her numbers are wrong on purpose. When she confronts Coach, he warns her to keep tallying. That night, cleaning out her grandmother's kitchen, she finds a recipe card titled 'Championship Casserole' with steps like 'fold in the crowd' and 'let rise until believed.' Emotional beat: the thrill of being needed curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Rigged Game
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with interludes from star player Marcus. Testing the recipe's instructions at practice, Hazel accidentally erases Marcus's injury history — and part of his memory of her. The team surges; the town glows too brightly, residents repeating the same conversations. Hazel realizes grandma didn't just cook: she fed the town its reality, and the recipe box is running out of pages. Emotional beat: guilt as Hazel sees what belonging costs others.

chapters.title: Fourth Quarter
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The incomplete final page demands 'one who chooses to be counted.' The rival school arrives — hollow-eyed players who lost their own recipe years ago. During the championship, Hazel discovers Coach has been feeding her rigged data to spare her the choice grandma once faced. With seconds left and the town literally dimming, Hazel takes the court herself, writing her name into the lineup. Emotional beat: terror becoming resolve.

chapters.title: Yearbook
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, weeks later. She wins the game but forfeits the ritual's protection: the town must now exist honestly, unglamorous and real, and Hazel's memories of grandma have thinned to a warm blur. Marcus remembers her fully; the team saves her a seat. In the empty gym, Hazel fills in the recipe box's blank final page with something new — not a spell, just a list of names, hers included. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into chosen belonging.
